transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-12-21
- Time: 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~55 minutes
- Attendees: Elena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Raman (Cobalt Head of ML), Samir Patel (Eng Manager), Jorge Velasquez (Security)

Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Redwood team walked through POC scope focused on cost modeling and unit economics for Cobalt's chat + embeddings workloads. Customer prioritized latency SLOs for triage chat (<=200ms tail) and unit cost budget (~$15k/month). Discussed workload sizing, expected qps, batching/caching knobs, dedicated vs hosted, timeline (2-4 week POC), benchmarks to run, and security/compliance gating items. Next steps and owners captured.

Transcript:
00:00 Elena Park: okay good afternoon everyone thanks for joining, i'll kick us off. um so today's goal is to scope the poc for cost modeling and unit economics for the triage chat plus embedding pipeline for cobalt, yep.
00:07 Dr. Priya Raman: thanks elena, yeah we want fairly concrete numbers — cost per 1k messages, per-embedding, and also options if we move to dedicated infra.
00:12 Marcus Chen: hi all, marcus from redwood, i'll own the benchmark setup and the perf side. quick q to start, priya, what's your expected p95/p99 latency target for the triage chat?
00:20 Dr. Priya Raman: ideally p95 < 200ms, p99 < 500ms. throughput is moderate — around 150 qps peak, average 40 qps across day, with spikes during release windows.
00:31 Samir Patel: to add, our budget for this project, at least initial pilot, is about $15k/month for inference costs; we can flex if the business case is strong but want to understand tradeoffs.
00:40 Jorge Velasquez: security gating — SOC2 is mandatory, encryption at rest w/ customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) or on-prem HSM, SSO/SAML integration, and audit logs. also data residency — most data must stay in us-west region.
00:53 Elena Park: great that's super helpful. we'll map 3 configs: hosted (redwood api), dedicated reserved capacity, and private vpc. we'll run throughput and latency benchmarks against your sample traffic and give per-token estimates.
01:05 Marcus Chen: first pass assumptions: model family you plan to use? large LLM? quantized?
01:10 Dr. Priya Raman: we evaluated multiple open models, leaning towards a 70B dense variant for intent classification and chat — we can test smaller 13B for latency comparisons. we can provide the model weights or use redwood-curated variant.
01:21 Marcus Chen: ok that helps. for cost modeling i'll surface three main levers: model size (affects token compute), batching settings (batch size e.g. 8-32), and KV/prefix caching for repeated contexts. quantization can reduce cost by ~2-3x for some ops depending on model.
01:33 Samir Patel: what's your rough per-token for hosted right now? ballpark.
01:36 Elena Park: ballpark numbers — hosted generation currently ranges ~$0.00025 to $0.0005 per token depending on model and context length; embeddings are in the low single-digit cents per 1k embeddings for our curated models — i'll send exacts in the spreadsheet. those numbers will change if you go dedicated; typically dedicated lowers per-token by ~20-50% depending on utilization and batching.
01:53 Jorge Velasquez: that's pretty wide. for budgeting we need examples: if we have 100k messages / month with avg 200 tokens/generation, what does that look like?
02:02 Marcus Chen: quick calc, using 200 tokens avg and $0.0003/token => 100k * 200 * 0.0003 = $6k/month for generation. embeddings separate — say 50k embeddings at $0.004 per embedding ~ $200/month. Then infra overhead and egress could add. but we'll put full model in sheet with hosted vs dedicated scenarios.
02:23 Dr. Priya Raman: nice. can you model worst-case spikes for release cadence where qps jumps to 400? we care about tail latency then.
02:29 Marcus Chen: yes we'll do steady-state and spike runs. for spikes we recommend a burst pool or autoscale config in dedicated. hosted has automatic routing/fallback that can move requests to compatible variants if capacity saturated.
02:40 Elena Park: also caching — your triage chat likely has repeated prompt prefixes (patient intake form templates). With prefix/KV cache we can often avoid re-evaluating the full context and reduce per-request tokens and compute. caching can drive 10-60% savings depending on cache hit rate.
02:55 Samir Patel: real question: how do batching knobs affect latency? if you increase batch size you improve throughput and reduce cost per token, but tail latency suffers?
03:03 Marcus Chen: exactly. batching is a trade. for low-latency triage we might keep batch size smaller (4-8) and rely more on caching; for async tasks we can batch to 32 or 64. Redwood Optimize will generate recommended batching profiles based on your traffic mix. we'll include 3 scenarios: latency optimized, cost optimized, balanced.
03:20 Dr. Priya Raman: for the POC benchmarks, we want to see p50/p95/p99, tokens/s, cost per 1k tokens, and CPU/GPU utilization. also a breakdown of where spend is (compute vs memory vs network).
03:33 Marcus Chen: agreed — we'll capture metrics and token-level cost. we'll run variants: quantized int8 vs fp16, dedicated GPUs (A100/RTX? we'll propose) vs hosted, and batching/caching toggles.
03:46 Jorge Velasquez: on security — if we go private, we need to know what control plane sits in redwood and what is customer-managed. can you send architecture diagrams and SOC2 docs?
03:54 Elena Park: yes we'll send an architectural note: private deployment options (VPC peering/privatelink and optionally on-prem bundle). SOC2 cert and audit logs example will be attached. we'll add KMS integration notes.
04:05 Samir Patel: timeline — how long to get meaningful results?
04:08 Marcus Chen: typical POC 2-4 weeks. week 1: onboarding and data/model handoff, week 2: benchmark runs and baseline numbers, week 3: optimization iterations (batching, caching, quant), week 4: final report and economics. we can compress if you want an accelerated 2-week pilot but that increases risk for thorough tuning.
04:26 Dr. Priya Raman: 3 weeks works for us. start ASAP after security doc review.
04:30 Elena Park: ok noted. budget note — if you start with hosted tests we can do most of the benchmarking without infra commitments; dedicated/dedicated reserved needs a bit more lead time and a commitment for reserved capacity. we'll show cost curves.
04:45 Samir Patel: curious — what's the unit economics for embeddings at scale? we foresee creating clinical embeddings for search across 10M records in the future.
04:53 Marcus Chen: embeddings at large scale change dynamics — throughput and batching are crucial. if you process offline batches, cost per embedding is mostly compute and you can get low per-embedding price with batching of hundreds to thousands. For realtime embeddings (API calls), latency matters and batching is smaller, so per-embedding is higher. we'll include both offline bulk and realtime pricing scenarios.
05:10 Dr. Priya Raman: also, any differences in model quality when quantizing? we need to track regression in our eval set.
05:16 Marcus Chen: yes quantization can introduce minor degradation depending on model; we'll run quality evals on your prompt set and flag regressions. Redwood Optimize suggests models/quantize combos with recommended thresholds.
05:26 Elena Park: little bit of housekeeping: we'll need a small sample dataset (anonymized) and a traffic replay or synthetics to run representative benchmarks. who will own that?
05:34 Samir Patel: we'll provide anonymized chat logs and a JSON traffic replay — samir to share link.
05:39 Jorge Velasquez: and i'll send the security constraints doc.
05:43 Dr. Priya Raman: ok. can you include a sensitivity analysis — e.g., if token length increases by 2x how cost changes, or if cache hit rate moves between 20-80%?
05:52 Marcus Chen: yes we'll include sensitivity scenarios. example quick callout: doubling average tokens doubles raw generation cost, but caching can reduce effective tokens by factor depending on hit rate, so the net isn't linear.
06:03 Elena Park: anything else?
06:05 Dr. Priya Raman: what about fallback strategies if capacity's constrained? we don't want degraded user experience.
06:10 Marcus Chen: Redwood supports smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants; we can set rules to route lower-priority requests to cheaper variants or to apply shorter context truncation. we'll demo canary rollouts and fallback policies in the poc if you'd like.
06:24 Samir Patel: one more — network egress charges? if we host in cloud with region constraints will egress to your analytics add a lot?
06:29 Elena Park: egress is usually minor compared to token compute for typical LLM workloads, but we'll include a line item. if you ingest large vector stores or move huge files it's different.
06:35 Dr. Priya Raman: ok great. let's recap next steps.
06:38 Elena Park: recap: (1) elena to send cost model spreadsheet, sample scenarios hosted vs dedicated vs private; (2) marcus to run benchmarks using your sample dataset in two modes (latency optimized and throughput); (3) jorge to share security/KMS/SOC2 expectations; (4) schedule follow-up week of 12/29 to review results. is that accurate?
06:54 Samir Patel: yes that's right.
06:56 Jorge Velasquez: yes.
06:58 Dr. Priya Raman: yep.
07:00 Elena Park: great thanks everyone. i'll follow up with calendar invite and attach the documents.
07:05 Marcus Chen: thanks all, bye.
07:07 (call ends)
